chunks: It is reported that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) wrote in his letter to Sahl ibn Hunayf (may God have mercy on him):

By Allah, I did not wrench the gate of Khaybar and throw it forty arm-lengths behind my back by physical strength nor by a regimen of nourishment. Rather, I was aided by a celestial power and a soul radiant with the light of its Lord. I am of Ahmad just as light is of light.

By Allah, had all the Arabs united against my fighting, I would not have fled; and had I been given the opportunity over their necks, none would have remained. He who does not care when his death descends upon him — his heart is steadfast in calamities.

This was narrated to me — along with the entirety of the letter containing this passage — by Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq (may God be pleased with him). He said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi narrated to us from Abu Bakr Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Hibbal al-Tabari. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Khashab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Muhsin narrated to us from Yunus ibn Thibyan from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them).

key_terms.الضوء من الضوء: Light from light — a metaphor for Ali's spiritual derivation from the Prophet Muhammad
key_terms.الملمات: Calamities, severe hardships that test one's resolve
key_terms.جنان: Heart (in classical Arabic, the inner heart/mind as seat of courage)
key_terms.قوة ملكوتية: Celestial/angelic power — divine empowerment beyond the physical realm

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about how he wrenched the gate of Khaybar?
ai.summary: This narration preserves a remarkable passage from a letter written by Imam Ali (peace be upon him) to his companion Sahl ibn Hunayf, in which he explains the miracle of the gate of Khaybar. Ali explicitly denies that his feat was accomplished through physical strength or diet, attributing it instead to a divine celestial power and his unique spiritual bond with the Prophet — expressed through the profound metaphor of being 'light from light.' The passage also contains a celebrated wisdom saying about the correlation between fearlessness in the face of death and steadfastness of heart in adversity. This letter was likely written during Ali's caliphate to explain the nature of Prophetic and Imamic miracles to his trusted companion.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: It is reported that Amir al-Mu’minin (as) wrote in his letter to Sahl b. Hanif (rh):

By Allah, I did not wrench the gate of Khaybar and throw it forty armlengths behind my back by the power of my body nor by a regimen. Rather, I was assisted by an angelic power and a soul illuminated by its Lord. I am of Ahmad just as light is of light.
By Allah, had the Arabs unified upon my killing, I would not flee, and had I been given a chance to strike their necks, none would remain. He who is awaited by Gardens does not mind death.

This was narrated to me along with its entire letter by Ahmad b. Musa al-Daqqaq (ra). He said: Muhammad b. Harun al-Sufi narrated to us from Abi Bakr `Ubaydullah b. Musa al-Hibal al-Tabari. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn al-Khashab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Muhsan narrated to us from Yunus b. Thibyan from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as).
